evaluation_categories: category - functional type: what the resource physically is (subagents, skills, hooks, mcp, cli-tool, marketplace, discovery-index)
automation_depth - orchestrated (routes/chains itself), manual-invoke (triggered on demand), or index-only (not installable itself)
token_footprint - lazy (loads on demand), mixed (partial always-loaded overhead), always-loaded, or n/a
tool_compatibility - which of our supported integrations (claude-code, cursor, codex) the resource actually targets
conflict_risk - chance of colliding with a generated Kit 1/Kit 2 agent, skill, or hook name, or double-firing a hook
license - confirm at install time when null here; do not assume permissive
pinned_ref - null until a project actually pins one; record it with install_open_source_kit.py --pin ID=REF
trust_flags - known-fake or inflated trust signals (e.g. a statistically implausible star count) that must not be read as endorsement; absent means no known issue

resources.name: Anthropic Official Plugin Marketplace
resources.description: Anthropic's own curated marketplace (~36 internal + ~220 external listings) - the safest first stop since Anthropic vets these before listing.
resources.token_footprint: n/a - depends on what is installed from it
resources.risk_notes: Listing is vetted by Anthropic, but each plugin still carries its own upstream code - review before installing, especially anything with hooks or network access.

resources.name: Anthropic Community Plugin Marketplace
resources.description: Read-only mirror of the community submission marketplace - centrally indexed but with lighter vetting than the official list.
resources.token_footprint: n/a - depends on what is installed from it
resources.risk_notes: Lower bar for listing than claude-plugins-official - treat as a discovery source, review each plugin individually.

resources.name: Model Context Protocol - Official Servers
resources.description: Official reference MCP server implementations (GitHub, filesystem, Postgres, Slack, etc.), maintained by the MCP steering group.
resources.token_footprint: mixed - each enabled server adds its tool schemas to every request; enable only what a project needs
resources.risk_notes: MCP is a protocol, not a single vendor - each server gets its own credentials/permission scope, review individually.

resources.name: wshobson/agents
resources.description: Multi-harness plugin marketplace (Claude Code/Codex/Cursor/OpenCode/Copilot/Antigravity): 202 agents, 181 skills, 105 commands, 93 plugins.
resources.token_footprint: mixed - large catalog, but plugin-based install lets you cherry-pick individual plugins instead of the whole set
resources.risk_notes: Large surface area - install only the specific agent/skill plugins a project actually needs, not the full catalog; check for name collisions with generated Kit 1/2 agents first.

resources.name: VoltAgent/awesome-claude-code-subagents
resources.description: 100+ subagents organized by category, each documenting an explicit minimal tool allowlist - a strong reference for least-privilege subagent design.
resources.token_footprint: lazy - copy in only the individual agent files a project needs
resources.risk_notes: Copy in individual agent .md files, not the whole tree - verify each agent's declared tools: allowlist before use.

resources.name: obra/superpowers (+ superpowers-skills)
resources.description: Well-regarded core skills library (TDD, debugging, collaboration patterns); listed in Anthropic's own official marketplace.
resources.verified_command: Inside a Claude Code session: `/plugin install superpowers@claude-plugins-official` - already listed in the official marketplace, no separate marketplace add needed.
resources.risk_notes: Passed Anthropic's own marketplace listing bar - the strongest trust signal in this catalog.

resources.name: ComposioHQ/awesome-claude-skills
resources.description: Large curated skills/plugins index from Composio (an established MCP/tooling vendor) - a discovery index, not a single installable resource.
resources.risk_notes: Vet whatever you find here with this same checklist before adding it.

resources.name: disler/claude-code-hooks-mastery
resources.description: The most commonly cited teaching repo for how Claude Code hooks actually work (PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop, security-blocking hooks, sub-agent orchestration patterns).
resources.token_footprint: n/a - reference/teaching repo, not meant to run wholesale
resources.risk_notes: Hooks are exactly the layer most likely to double-fire against our own enforcement hooks - read and adapt individual scripts rather than installing the whole hook set.

resources.name: davila7/claude-code-templates
resources.description: CLI for scaffolding/configuring/monitoring a Claude Code setup from templates.
resources.token_footprint: n/a - affects what gets written into project config, not a per-request context cost by itself
resources.risk_notes: Can write into existing project config - review every file it proposes before accepting.

resources.name: hesreallyhim/awesome-claude-code
resources.description: The most established general 'awesome list' for the ecosystem (slash commands, CLAUDE.md examples, workflows, tooling); running since April 2025.
resources.risk_notes: Discovery only - vet each linked resource individually.

resources.name: punkpeye/awesome-mcp-servers
resources.description: Long-running (since November 2024), broad MCP server directory.
resources.risk_notes: Directory only, no vetting implied by inclusion - review each linked server individually.

resources.name: Graphify-Labs/graphify
resources.description: Parses a codebase (code, docs, SQL schemas, configs, PDFs) into a local, deterministic knowledge graph via tree-sitter AST parsing; a /graphify skill for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and Gemini CLI, no vector store.
resources.token_footprint: mixed - large per-query token reduction claimed after an expensive one-time graph build (hours) plus incremental rebuilds (~10 min)
trust_flags: implausible star count: 112,842 stars / 10,980 forks at ~5 months old (created 2026-04-03, verified via GitHub API 2026-08-31) - matches the fake-star pattern in arXiv 2412.13459; previously excluded from this catalog for this exact reason
resources.risk_notes: HIGH RISK - re-added after prior exclusion for a statistically implausible star count; flagged, not vetted for trust. Its strict-mode install adds a PreToolUse hook that intercepts file-search tool calls - test interaction with our own local-context.sh/subagent-gate.sh on a throwaway branch before rollout. Functionally overlaps the Local Context Engine's FTS5/BM25 retrieval - run the same query set through both before treating both as necessary. Pin to an exact commit SHA; do not track a floating branch.

resources.name: JuliusBrussee/caveman
resources.description: Token-compression skill/CLI/MCP toolkit that rewrites agent and subagent output into a terse compressed form to cut token usage.
resources.token_footprint: mixed - claims net token reduction but adds its own always-on MCP/proxy component to the pipeline
resources.license: MIT (skill/adoption surfaces); BSL-1.1 (core engine/runtime) - mixed, confirm per-component compatibility with client work-for-hire terms
trust_flags: implausible star count: 101,968 stars / 5,933 forks at ~5 months old (created 2026-04-04, verified via GitHub API 2026-08-31) - matches the fake-star pattern in arXiv 2412.13459
resources.risk_notes: HIGH RISK - star count implausible for repo age; added despite this by explicit decision, not because trust was established. Ships a curl|bash installer and an always-on proxy that rewrites tool output before it reaches the model - read install.sh in full and pin to an exact commit SHA; do not run the one-liner unpinned. BSL-1.1 on the core engine is not fully open-source.

resources.name: grill-me (mattpocock/skills)
resources.description: A single skill within a larger personal skills collection: interviews the user about a plan/design branch-by-branch until every open decision is forced explicit.
resources.token_footprint: lazy - single skill file; do not import the surrounding ~40-skill collection wholesale
trust_flags: implausible star count: 242,415 stars / 20,609 forks at ~7 months old (created 2026-02-03, verified via GitHub API 2026-08-31) - more stars than facebook/react accumulated in 12 years; matches the fake-star pattern in arXiv 2412.13459
resources.risk_notes: HIGH RISK - the most extreme star/age ratio of any candidate reviewed for this catalog; added despite this by explicit decision. Copy in only the grill-me skill file, not the surrounding collection. Check for overlap with any existing clarifying-interview/planning skill before installing alongside one.

resources.name: Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-claudecode
resources.description: Multi-agent orchestration plugin advertising 19 specialized agents and 39 skills with an 'Ultrawork' mode for maximized parallel/automatic task execution.
resources.token_footprint: always-loaded - 19 agent + 39 skill descriptors add fixed routing overhead every session regardless of use; measure before adopting (scripts/context_budget.py)
trust_flags: implausible star count: 38,913 stars / 3,491 forks at ~7.5 months old (created 2026-01-09, verified via GitHub API 2026-08-31) - matches the fake-star pattern in arXiv 2412.13459, less extreme than the other three added here but still disqualifying as a trust signal
resources.risk_notes: HIGH RISK on two independent axes: (1) star count implausible for age; (2) a 19-agent self-orchestrating architecture is exactly what Symfony's subagent-gate.sh + CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH=1 + denied Agent(Explore/Plan/general-purpose) is designed to block by default. Will not function without an explicit roster-whitelist decision (see the Kit1/Kit2 collision analysis - same fork in the road as `ecc`). At least 6 other 'oh-my-claude*' forks exist with ordinary star counts - confirm this specific fork is the one intended before installing.
